summary: Iteration_2 end-to-end tests: 25/25 backend pytest cases pass and 8/8 UI flows pass. Verified lead scoring (single + score-all with AI, persistence check), AI Agent plan/approve/reject with actual DB stage change on update_deal, sequences CRUD + toggle + delete, sequence enroll → AI-drafted PENDING message, REAL email send via Resend (delivery='email sent via Resend'), WhatsApp mocked ('simulated — no real send'), message reject, team invite with real email send (email_sent=true), invite verify + accept flow creating a REP user in same workspace, and comprehensive RBAC: rep sees 0 records/stats, gets 403 on /team and /invites, gets [] on messages/pending. UI: Deals kanban shows close-score badges + next-best-action lines after Score all, Approvals shows agent-action cards and pending message cards with approve/reject wired, Sequences builder saves and enrollment creates approval-gated message, Team page invite works. Accept-invite page renders both loading and invalid-token states.

issues: Left column continues to show 'Verifying your invitation…' subtitle even after right column shows 'Invitation is invalid or expired'. Minor — subtitle should update to reflect error state.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py grew from 800 → 1305 lines with iteration_2. Splitting into routers (auth, records, ai, sequences, invites, agent) is now overdue for maintainability.

score-all endpoint runs LLM calls serially in a loop (async for + await inside) — for larger workspaces (>20 open deals) this will exceed request timeouts. Consider asyncio.gather or a background job.
approve_message raises 502 with str(e) on Resend failure — this can leak internal error details to the client; safer to log full error and return a sanitized message.
In Sequences.jsx enroll dialog the <option> element contains a wrapped <span> (Emergent x-* instrumentation) causing a React hydration warning in console. Not functional but shows in console.error.

AI actions from /agent/plan are stored with actor_id=user['id']; the /approve endpoint does not re-check that the approving user is the same actor or a manager. Any workspace member can approve any pending action. Consider restricting to actor OR manager.
score-all does not update _score for Won/Lost deals but also doesn't clear stale _score on records that recently moved to Won/Lost — cards can display stale AI scores after stage changes.
seed_data_creation: Tests created several TEST_* sequences (cleaned up), one invited rep user (delivered+rep_*@resend.dev) which remains logged in the DB — safe/idempotent. Real emails were sent to Resend's deliverable delivered+*@resend.dev inbox (test-only sink). Backend tests also triggered agent update_deal actions which moved 'VertexPay — Expansion' from Lead → Contacted (visible in Deals kanban).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Two backend test files: backend_test.py (iteration_1 baseline, 18 tests) + test_iteration2.py (iteration_2 features, 25 tests). Run both with: pytest /app/backend/tests/ -v. AI tests take ~25s (score-all loops over deals sequentially). Invite tests send real emails via Resend proxy — recipients MUST be delivered+*@resend.dev. WhatsApp is intentionally mocked. Agent actions test approves an update_deal so demo deal stages will drift over repeated runs (Lead deal moves to Contacted or similar).
